newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania cuts reserve requirement by half - report.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania cuts reserve requirement by half - report.

text.p: The Bank of Tanzania (BOT) has halved its Statutary Minimum Reserve (SMR) requirement for commercial banks, the bank said.
In a statement obtained on Thursday, the BOT said it would cut SMR to six percent from 12 percent, effective January 20.
"Every bank is required to maintain minimum reserves equivalent to 6.0 percent of the outstanding balance of its total shilling deposits and borrowings from the general public.

"For the purpose of this circular, the reserves required of every bank shall consist of the balance of its "Statutary Minimum Reserve' account maintained by each bank with the bank," the statement said.
The decision to cut the SMR was made without any public announcement by the BOT's governor, Idris Rashidi.
A senior official from an international lending institution said the SMR decision could lead to higher inflation.
"This is a major decision. It's a major reduction. At the same time that you're pumping purchasing power into the public, how do you reduce your inflation?"
Tanzania's annual inflation rate is running at 16.2 percent, down from 18.8 percent in October. The BOT said a further reduction in inflation to 15 percent could be expected for December.
